caption: The drawing features a repeating floral and avian motif rendered in brown ink on a beige or light tan background. In the central part of the composition, there is a large bird, possibly a peacock or other similar bird, depicted with outstretched wings and detailed linear patterns on its wings and body. The bird is surrounded by an array of densely packed flowers and foliage, with many curling stems and blossoms filling the surrounding space. In the upper left corner, a partial circular motif, possibly the sun or a medallion with a scalloped edge, encroaches into the floral field, decorated with smaller flower patterns inside. The overall composition is intricate, with all spaces between the main subjects filled in with leaf and flower designs, creating a sense of ornate density. The color palette is limited to shades of brown set against the neutral background.
title: Handwoven Coverlet
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
